questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get better at french and therefore chose a french-speaking destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not entirely simple. Generally speaking, i found the website of Sorbonne University hard to navigate, and I had to send several emails to completely understand the process of choosing courses etc. The people responsible were helpful, but i think it was hard for them to understand to what point the country's education system is different from ours and therefore to what extent the administrative approached where hard to understand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a meeting where the proceedings where presented, and that was pretty much it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very simple - I got housing at the Foundation Danoise. But generally i know that it is very difficult to find affordable housing in the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is not an option.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont have any info to add as i do not know the student-housing options.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very complicated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Choosing courses consisted in creating your own schedule and making sure that everything made sense with timetables and ECTS points. As an Erasmus student I wanted to take courses from different departments, which was indeed possible, but very difficult as the pedagogical inscriptions are  done in a different way in every department. In the literature and language department it is done by hand in a room at a specific time, whereas it in others consists in an excel arc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration was pretty helpful on email, but you have to figure out who to contact on your own, and you will often get forwarded to other people.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. Unfortunately some things weren't possible because of timetable conflicts, but the university was definitely not at fault.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay calm. Ask questions. Understand what courses you would like to take before going, and if you want to take courses outside your own department, start sending emails a few weeks in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had about half of my classes on a bachelor level and the rest on master. I actually found the master level courses easier and more approachable, as there is less focus on methodology, and they are often more interesting. Would recommend.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Generally very different. Less pedagogical.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Take a million language classes before going. Everything depends on your french. 
2) Get used to writing in hand. 
3) See in advance if you know anyone in the city who can give you a helping hand and introduce you to people. If not idk.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Learn to write polite emails in french. This will be useful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The wonderful friends i made. And speaking french.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking french. Writing in french.
